note: M1 (M3 source). Core fork: deep learning / Boltzmann machine (physics: learn the constraint network) vs KRR / CSP (mathematical logic: given fundamental constraints reasoned about). Introduces constraint networks and propagation.

entities.name: representation
entities.definition: A schema that exposes the natural constraints inherent in a problem, making important objects and their spatial relations explicit so that credit assignment largely goes away.

entities.name: constraint
entities.definition: Any restriction on the values of a variable, or on the relations among variables; a description of a stable regularity an agent can exploit to simplify a representation.

entities.name: constraint network
entities.definition: A graph whose nodes are variables and whose links are constraints among them; a search tree is a highly restricted special case where the only links are sequential.

entities.name: principle of locality
entities.definition: The finding that higher-order constraints can usually be reduced to binary ones, so an agent need only process information about local (two-variable) interdependencies — the fundamental reason representations are valuable for intelligence.

entities.name: propagation
entities.definition: Sending information across the links of a constraint network; information about one constraint becomes rich intermediate feedback for neighboring constraints.

entities.name: constraint satisfaction problem
entities.definition: A representation-informed search (e.g. Sudoku, scheduling): interleave propagation with a search heuristic (backtracking, forward-checking) to find an assignment that satisfies a set of given constraints.

entities.name: causal net
entities.definition: Pearl's Bayesian network: a directed acyclic graph whose constraints are conditional probabilities between parent and child variables; structure is given, probabilities are 'learned' by gathering information to test cause-effect beliefs.

entities.name: Boltzmann machine
entities.definition: Hinton's foundational building block of deep learning: an undirected, densely-interdependent network of binary variables whose soft-constraint correlations ('weights') are learned to minimize cost, yielding a probability distribution ('representation learning').

entities.name: deep learning
entities.definition: The currently-dominant AI paradigm built on Boltzmann-machine-style learning of correlations among units of Shannon information; treats intelligence as reducible to simple statistical mechanisms over homogeneous parts.

entities.name: Geoff Hinton
entities.definition: Deep-learning leader who invented the Boltzmann machine, named for the physicist Boltzmann; holds a 'physics' view that intelligence reduces to a few statistical laws over simple parts.

relations.evidence: Given the right representation, challenges of assigning credit to complex action sequences largely go away.
Representations are built out of sets of constraints on problem-solving environments.
The links of a constraint network are constraints among variables.
Because most constraints reduce to binary ones, information can be propagated locally instead of combinatorially.
Propagating information across constraints provides feedback that avoids combinatorial search.
A CSP is a representation-informed search.
Causal nets are a type of constraint network.
Boltzmann machines are a type of constraint network.
Forward-checking interleaves a search action with constraint propagation.
Constraint propagation sends updated probabilities through the directed acyclic graph.
Boltzmann variables are binary (1,0) as in Shannon information; learning is a type of compression.
The essential ideas behind deep learning are captured by Hinton's Boltzmann machines.
The essential ideas behind deep learning are captured by Hinton's Boltzmann machines.
The KRR perspective in AI is the one implied by CSPs (constraints given, reasoned about).

claims.proposition: A good representation exposes the natural constraints inherent in a problem, making objects and their relations explicit so the problem becomes easy to solve and credit assignment largely goes away.

Any complex problem can be defined as variables, domains, and constraints; by the principle of locality higher-order constraints usually reduce to binary ones, so an agent processes only local interdependencies and avoids combinatorial complexity.

Propagation — sending information across the links of a constraint network — turns information about one constraint into rich intermediate feedback for neighbors, which is the power of representation over searching a tree (Sudoku, crosswords).
claims.conditions: the network has enough connected constraints to propagate across

claims.proposition: A constraint satisfaction problem is a representation-informed search: interleave propagation with a search heuristic (backtracking, forward-checking) to satisfy a set of given constraints.
claims.conditions: constraints are given and the goal is usually a single solution

claims.proposition: In a causal net (Bayesian network) the constraints are conditional probabilities between parent and child variables in a directed acyclic graph; the structure is given but the probabilities are learned by gathering information, like a scientist testing hypotheses.
claims.conditions: the causal structure can be specified in advance

claims.proposition: A Boltzmann machine learns soft-constraint correlations (weights) among binary input/output variables in an undirected, densely-interdependent network, yielding a probability distribution; it is the foundational building block of deep learning and embodies a 'physics' view of intelligence as a few statistical laws over homogeneous parts.
claims.conditions: abundant input-output data; generalization without defining the problem

claims.proposition: On the knowledge-representation-and-reasoning view implied by CSPs, intelligence is satisfying some given, fundamental constraints (algebra, geometry, accounting) to construct new ones — so causal nets and Boltzmann machines are just two specialized constraints among the diversity needed for general intelligence.
claims.conditions: constraints are fundamental and reasoned-from, not learned

tensions.dimension: where constraints come from and what intelligence is: learned correlations among homogeneous units (the physics hypothesis) vs. given, meaningful constraints satisfied and elaborated (the knowledge-representation-and-reasoning hypothesis)
tensions.conditions_a: The deep-learning / physics view fits when you have abundant input-output data and want generalization without defining the problem: learn a probability distribution (weights) over a directionless, densely-connected network, with no need to specify parents/children or the problem itself.
tensions.conditions_b: The KRR view fits when constraints are fundamental and given (algebra, geometry, accounting, scheduling) and intelligence is reasoning from them: satisfy and construct constraints with precision, interpretability, and elaboration tolerance.

probes.prompt: What makes solving Sudoku by constraint propagation fundamentally different from cracking a safe by trying combinations? Explain constraints, the principle of locality, and propagation in your answer.
expected_signals: Frames the safe as pure search (no informative links between guesses) and Sudoku as a constraint network with informative links.
Defines a constraint as a restriction on variable values/relations the agent can exploit.
Invokes the principle of locality: higher-order constraints reduce to binary ones, so reasoning stays local.
Explains propagation: information about one constraint becomes feedback for neighbors, avoiding combinatorial search.
